subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The equations ax+by+c=0 and lx+my+n=0 represent one and the same straight line, and r=l/a=n/c. Write the value of r in terms of m and b.

mark_split.label: Read r off the middle ratio

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what it means for two equations to be the same line, and where m and b sit in that statement.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the same-line condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two equations describe one line only when one is a non-zero multiple of the other, so all three coefficient ratios are equal.
steps.memory_tip: One line, one multiplier: l/a = m/b = n/c is the same number written three times.
lines: (1) and (2) are one and the same line,
l/a = m/b = n/c   (a, b, c all non-zero)

recall.must_convey: That the same line forces l/a = m/b = n/c.
accept: l by a equals m by b equals n by c
one equation is a multiple of the other

steps.why: Multiplying an equation by a non-zero number does not change the line it describes, and that is the only way two equations can describe the same line, so every coefficient is scaled by the one same factor.
common_mistakes: Equating only two of the three ratios and stopping there.
Pairing l with b and m with a instead of matching like with like.

steps.label: Read r off the middle ratio
steps.margin_note: Second mark. r is defined as the common ratio, and m/b is that same common ratio, so the answer is one line.
steps.memory_tip: r is the common ratio, so r equals whichever of the three ratios you are asked for.
lines: So r is the common ratio of the chain,
and m/b is that same common ratio.

recall.must_convey: That r = m/b, because m/b is the same common ratio as l/a and n/c.
accept: m over b is the same common ratio
the middle ratio is also r

steps.why: The question already names two of the three equal ratios as r, so the third is r as well; nothing has to be solved.
common_mistakes: Writing r = b/m, with the ratio upside down.
Answering with l/a again instead of the ratio the question asks for.
